‘Sometimes to love is to let go’, former Man Utd midfielder announces retirement

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata has declared his retirement from professional football at the age of 38, bringing an end to a beautiful career of around 20 years.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Spaniard went on to win one of the biggest trophies in professional football.
  • Recent findings suggest that mata enjoyed a memorable spell at Manchester United after arriving from Chelsea in January 2014.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata has declared his retirement from professional football at the age of 38, bringing an end to a beautiful career of around 20 years.

Recent findings suggest that the Spaniard went on to win one of the biggest trophies in professional football. The former Manchester United midfielder confirmed his decision on Wednesday after ending his playing career with Australian side Melbourne Victory.

Recent findings suggest that mata enjoyed a memorable spell at Manchester United after arriving from Chelsea in January 2014. He spent more than eight years at Old Trafford, making 285 appearances, scoring 51 goals and winning four trophies.

In a recent development, his first trophy with Manchester United came in the 2016 FA Cup final against Crystal Palace. He also helped the club win the Community Shield, League Cup and Europa League during the 2016/17 campaign.

Sources indicate that before moving to Manchester, Juan Mata had established himself as one of Chelsea’s most creative players. He won the club’s Player of the Year award in both of his first two full seasons at Stamford Bridge before eventually joining United as David Moyes’ marquee signing.

Recent findings suggest that mata probably had the biggest moments of his career in the Spain shirt. He earned 41 international caps and scored 10 goals, becoming part of the most talented Spanish team in history. He went on to win the 2010 FIFA World Cup and Euro 2012 with Spain while etching his name in Spanish football history with a goal in Spain’s 4-0 victory over Italy in the European Championship final.

After leaving Manchester United in 2022, the midfielder continued his career with Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before joining Melbourne Victory in September 2025.

It has been revealed that his final season in Australia was an impressive one. Mata registered five goals and 13 assists, won the Johnny Warren Medal and earned a place in the A-League Team of the Season.

Sources indicate that sometimes, to love… is to let go. THANKS FOOTBALL. ⚽️❤️♾️A veces, amar… es dejar ir. GRACIAS FÚTBOL. ⚽️❤️♾️ pic.twitter.com/v7otd6AyOq.

Reflecting on his decision, Mata spoke about the reason that kept him playing for so many years.

“I was able to keep going for so many years because of the sheer joy of playing,” he said.

He also made it clear that retirement would not mean walking away from football altogether.

Sources indicate that “Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game.”.

According to recent reports, manchester United also paid tribute to their former midfielder, writing on social media: “Great player, better person. Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan.”.

Great player, better person.Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan ❤️.

Recent findings suggest that mata leaves the game on his own terms and more importantly as a winner. With all the trophies he won, United will remember him for a lot more. The persona he had, the brilliant assists, goals like that one on Anfield and more importantly the joy he brough to United fans in a difficult time at the club.

Telstar vs PEC Zwolle - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:40.
  • Matchday 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie season sees Telstar host PEC Zwolle at BUKO Stadion on Saturday evening.
  • Both teams begin this weekend’s clash within three points of the automatic relegation places, and neither will want to leave empty-handed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:40.

Matchday 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie season sees Telstar host PEC Zwolle at BUKO Stadion on Saturday evening.

Both teams begin this weekend’s clash within three points of the automatic relegation places, and neither will want to leave empty-handed.

A 10-match winless run between August 8 and October 23 dampened any optimism that may have been brewing after Telstar’s season-opening win over NEC. However, they have since responded with four points from a possible six, most recently earning a 2-2 draw against Fortuna Sittard.

Having been tipped by many as the next managerial casualty of 2026-27, Henk Brugge appears to have bought himself some breathing room, but he will know his position remains precarious, and any underwhelming result could still spell the end for him.

Averaging two goals per home league match this term, De Witte Leeuwen have found little difficulty scoring in front of their fans, although much of that good work is being undone by a porous defence that has conceded 17 times across six home games.

January’s 4-1 defeat marked Telstar’s seventh straight loss against Zwolle and extended their winless run in this fixture to 16 matches across all competitions dating back to February 2007. This weekend’s hosts will need to buck an unpleasant trend to secure all three points.

A 4-2 triumph over FC Utrecht in their most recent home match ended a run of six games without a win for Telstar, who now seek back-to-back victories in Velsen for the first time since beating Sparta Rotterdam and Heracles by a combined score of 7-1 to close out 2025-26 on a high.

Recent findings suggest that after weeks of searching, PEC Zwolle will have a new face in the dugout for their upcoming clash against Telstar, with Alex Pastoor recently appointed as head coach until the end of the 2026-27 season. He replaces Henry van der Vegt, whose 15-month tenure ended in October.

Pastoor’s immediate task will be to build on his side’s four-game league unbeaten run, during which they have collected eight points from a possible 12, with only Heerenveen (12) and Ajax (10) boasting a better record in the division.

With three of their next four matches coming against teams at the moment in the top seven - AZ Alkmaar, Fortuna Sittard, and PSV Eindhoven - De Blauwvingers could use a win here as they look to put some distance between themselves and the drop zone before the end of 2026.

Sources indicate that both of Saturday’s opponents have managed just three clean sheets between them from 24 matches this season, so this weekend’s clash is likely to be decided at the attacking end. On that front, Zwolle have struggled compared to their hosts, scoring five fewer goals so far.

However, the visitors could tilt things in their favour with a quick start, and having scored the opener in four of the last five gameweeks, they may look to capitalise on a Telstar side that has conceded first four times during that span.

Telstar form (all competitions):.

PEC Zwolle form (all competitions):.

Gerald Alders, 21, has missed Telstar’s last four matches and will remain sidelined for Saturday’s clash as he continues his recovery to full fitness.

Rui Mendes is also unlikely to feature for the hosts, though his comeback is not far off after missing the last three matches.

Tyrone Owusu has four goals and one assist in his last six outings, already making this his most productive season in a Telstar shirt.

Deadline-day loan signing Filip Krastev has yet to feature this term due to an Achilles tendon injury sustained while playing for Goztepe.

Givaro Rahajaan and Sherel Floranus are also unavailable this weekend, but both are nearing their respective returns.

Telstar possible starting lineup:.

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Ahmed, Rossen; Martha, Owusu, Brouwer; Thorisson.

PEC Zwolle possible starting lineup:.

Schendelaar; Van der Haar, Viergever, Velthuis, Aertssen; Sommer, Thomas; Mbayo, Namli, Van der Wal; Van Hooijdonk.

Both teams have performed well of late, and neither enters Saturday’s game with their confidence depleted.

With little to separate the sides, a draw appears the most likely outcome, so we are backing a share of the spoils.

Manchester United could make an ambitious move for former Liverpool sporting director Michael Edwards, with the Glazer family reportedly keen to bring the highly rated executive to Old Trafford.

According to a report from popular Indykaila News on X, the Glazer side of United’s ownership wants Michael Edwards to take full control of the club’s football operations.

Recent findings suggest that exclusive: Manchester United board member eyes extraordinary move for Michael EdwardsA Manchester United board member is pushing for the appointment of former Liverpool director of football Michael Edwards. With the Glazers interested in the appointment, such a move would be a major shift from the current arrangement at Old Trafford, where Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS are currently responsible for overseeing the football department.

Edwards is regarded as one of the most influential executives in modern English football, having played a major role in building Liverpool’s squad under Jurgen Klopp.

Michael Edwards joined Liverpool in 2011 before being appointed as their sporting director in November 2016. He oversaw player recruitment bring in some of the biggest names at Liverpool including Mo Salah and Sadio Mane. Liverpool saw one of their most successful years in modern history in the Premier League and Europe under Jurgen Klopp while Edwards oversaw the footballing operations.

Manchester United have previously attempted to bring Edwards to Old Trafford before, but were unsuccessful.

According to recent reports, following his departure from Liverpool in 2022, Edwards turned down approaches from several clubs, including Manchester United and Chelsea. He then returned to Fenway Sports Group in March 2024 to oversee FSG’s wider football operations.

Sources indicate that his second spell with FSG came to an end in July 2026. That exit has reopened the door for many interested clubs including Manchester United. However, there is no confirmation that Edwards is considering another move to United.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament upgrade confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

According to recent reports, the concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

According to recent reports, caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Enzo brings a different tension.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Then there is the defensive side.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to initiative around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

It has been revealed that enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea.
  • Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation.
  • Recent findings suggest that that matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that that matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F.

In a recent development, the easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the crucial detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

According to recent reports, that is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

The Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive looks, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

In a recent development, one is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

According to recent reports, the other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

Sources indicate that the complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness challenges, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

Palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

Recent findings suggest that this is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

If Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United parted ways with Michael Carrick after a disastrous start to the Premier League season with just one win from 10 games.

Manchester United have spent a reported 12 million to bring Mauricio Pochettino and his coaching team from the United States to Old Trafford, with the Argentine determined to work alongside several familiar faces.

United paid around $10 million to secure Pochettino’s release from the US team and with a further $2 million reportedly required to secure members of his backroom staff.

It has been revealed that the 54-year-old has built a close working relationship with his coaching team throughout spells at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. Several of those staff members have followed him to Manchester United.

Jesus Perez is Pochettino’s long-time assistant and is widely regarded as his right-hand man. Their relationship began at Espanyol, where Perez initially worked as an analyst before becoming his assistant at Southampton. He has followed the Argentine throughout his career with spells at Tottenham, PSG and USA. He is now set to take the same role at Old Trafford.

Jimenez will work as United’s goalkeeping coach. He first joined Pochettino’s coaching setup at Espanyol in 2011 and has remained alongside him throughout his managerial career, including their time in England, France and the United States.

It has been revealed that the manager’s 31-year-old son has also joined the coaching group. Sebastiano started working with his father during their time at Tottenham and has continued as a sports scientist and fitness coach with him with the USA team. He is also joining Pochettino at Manchester United.

It has been revealed that the former Argentine defender has worked with Pochettino since his first managerial job at Espanyol. He has been involved in training sessions, video analysis and tactical preparation, helping the manager develop game looks.

The arrivals mean a major change behind the scenes at Carrington following the departures of Michael Carrick and his coaching staff.

Mauricio Pochettino is set to face Liverpool in his first game as Manchester United head coach on Sunday.

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

According to recent reports, pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the fresh manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha stated, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

“Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”.

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one massive problem for Pochettino.

Rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United. Highlighting a major problem, Smith said, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”.

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

Mauricio Pochettino has explained the importance of 'creating the culture' at Manchester United, as the Argentine looks to build a positive environment following his arrival as head coach.

The 54-year-old will take charge of his first Man United match on Sunday afternoon, when the 20-time English champions tackle Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino officially started work as Red Devils head coach on Wednesday, having flown straight to England after managing his final USA game against Haiti.

The South American has taken charge of a team that currently sit down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up just eight points from their first 10 games of the season.

Recent findings suggest that “It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free," Pochettino told Man United's official website.

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most vital thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

"When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

Industry observers note that “That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero. I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.

“To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create. We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.

Recent findings suggest that “The best squad that we can have are the players that we have and we need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players.

In a recent development, "We need to provide all the tools for them to perform. It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the facility to translate all their talent on the field.”.

Pochettino's training session on Thursday included both Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu, with the defensive duo both in line to be available against Liverpool.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United sitting in an unfamiliar 18th in the Premier League table with only one win from 10 matches. He has a massive job ahead of him, with many pundits and former players terming his situation the toughest in the Premier League.

Gary Neville believes the Argentine will need several transfer windows to get the squad where he wants it, if he gets that much of time at Manchester United.

The former captain shared his views on which players he expects Pochettino to keep, and who could be heading for the exit.

Industry observers note that neville believes Senne Lammens should remain part of the plans, although he expects Pochettino to bring in another goalkeeper to give him some competition for his place. At the back, he backed Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro to stay, while suggesting Ayden Heaven needs a loan move to the Championship.

“Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in,” Neville remarked on Stick to Football.

It has been revealed that in midfield, Neville wants Pochettino to build around Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. He also believes Andrey Santos could have a future at the club because of his age, mobility and aggression.

Industry observers note that mason Mount, however, is not part of his looks. Neville noted: “Mount would have to go” and identified him as the player to leave from that midfield group.

Neville also has his doubts on the forward line, with much of the front line seeing a change. Gary Neville expects Joshua Zirkzee to leave and believes United cannot continue paying Marcus Rashford’s wages.

Recent findings suggest that “Zirkzee definitely to go. I think Marcus 100 per cent to go because he’s on massive money and that story has been well told. They can’t afford to pay him that money, you have to get rid of that wage at the earliest opportunity.”.

He expects Pochettino to work with Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko. Patrick Dorgu could also be useful in the short term, although Neville thinks he may leave within the next couple of years. Manuel Ugarte, meanwhile, was another player he was certain would go.

Talking about the exits, Gary Neville has singled out many United stars to be shown the door in the first wave of squad clearance by Mauricio Pochettino. Neville identified Lisandro Martínez, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui as further candidates to leave in the first wave of departures, alongside Mount, Rashford and Zirkzee.

Recent findings suggest that neville believes another group of exits could follow a year later, with Shaw, Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Fernandes among the players whose futures may not be at the club in long term. Pochettino would also have to decide whether Santos and Carlos Baleba fit into his long-term plans.

Neville does not expect United to rebuild the squad in a single summer, even if Pochettino makes a positive start.

In a recent development, “But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.”.

It has been revealed that pochettino’s first game comes against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. His immediate priority will be to get some results for Manchester United but beyond the immediate games and results, Manchester United are expected to make multiple exits from the club as Pochettino settles into the job.

Joao Pedro missed Chelsea’s 3-0 Premier League defeat to Brentford with a knee problem, and the injury has since ruled him out of Brazil’s squad for the friendlies against Australia and India.

He was absent from Xabi Alonso’s confirmed lineups against Brentford, with Chelsea turning to other forward options instead.

Industry observers note that brazil’s coaching staff confirmed the withdrawal, pointing to the same knee issue that kept him out of the derby. Chelsea have not set a firm return date for Joao Pedro, leaving supporters to wait for further updates during the international break.

The Joao Pedro injury situation took a latest turn when the Standard reported that he is seeing a specialist during the international break to speed up his recovery.

According to the Standard, the forward is using this pause in the calendar to get ahead of the problem rather than wait for Chelsea to resume domestic action.

Chelsea have not issued their own statement on the specialist visit, and the club’s official line on Joao Pedro’s fitness remains limited to his withdrawal from matchday duty.

Full detail on the reported treatment can be found in football.london’s reported injury update, which first carried the specialist claim alongside Xabi Alonso’s comments on the striker’s season.

Until Chelsea confirm otherwise, the Standard’s report stands as the clearest picture of how the club are handling the knee concern.

It suggests a measured approach, with recovery prioritised over rushing Joao Pedro back into contention for the next fixture.

Before the injury forced him out, Xabi Alonso had made his admiration for Joao Pedro clear. The Chelsea manager ranked the forward among the Premier League’s elite strikers, alongside Manchester City’s Erling Haaland.

“If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I’m sure that João is there, Haaland for sure is there.

In a recent development, “So I would rate him that way. He has a very strong goal this year: to have a great season, to score many goals, and to be a nominee for not just this month but more months. I am not surprised, but really happy with the kind of player that we have here with João.”.

With Joao Pedro sidelined, Alonso must lean again on the depth built into his squad.

His approach to rotation, part of the squad management this season, faces another test while his in-form forward is unavailable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fernandes has been one of United’s most influential players since arriving from Sporting CP in January 2020.

Bruno Fernandes has scored 113 goals in 341 appearances for Manchester United and has regularly carried the creative responsibility in midfield for the Red Devils.

His performances have remained amazing despite United struggling in recent times. Despite a sluggish start to the last season, Bruno Fernandes went on to register 21 Premier League assists, breaking the league’s single-season record.

Mauricio Pochettino will now have the opportunity to speak directly with the midfielder and make his own case for him to remain part of the project.

However, there are several problems still to resolve. The financial terms, length of the proposed contract and release clause will all need to be discussed before an agreement can be reached with the Portuguese midfielder.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing to hold talks with Bruno Fernandes over his Manchester United future, with the club captain yet to agree a new contract at Old Trafford.

In a recent development, according to Fabrizio Romano, the new United head coach will now become involved in discussions with the Portuguese midfielder, whose current deal expires at the end of the season. The club have the option to extend it by a further 12 months, but are also keen to secure a longer-term agreement.

Manchester United have already held negotiations with Fernandes, but the 32-year-old has rejected two contract offers. Romano explained that Pochettino’s involvement could be an crucial part of the talks, although the final decision will rest with Bruno Fernandes and United.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano said: “First point: Mauricio Pochettino will be involved now in discussions with Bruno Fernandes.

“So, Pochettino will talk to Bruno, and he’s going to enter into this conversation.

“Then it’s going to be on Bruno, it’s going to be on the club.

“It’s a financial point, length of the contract, the release clause.

“It’s not Pochettino deciding yes or not, but Pochettino will be another factor now in the conversation.

“Then it’s on Bruno to decide.”.

Fernandes’ future is not settled at Manchester United and with Pochettino arriving at the club, he may have a different thought about his contract situation. Although a deal is not finalized yet but the talks will give the new head coach a chance to understand Fernandes’ position. However, the final call remains with Bruno Fernandes.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

The video offered supporters an early glimpse of Mauricio Pochettino working with his latest squad, but its release quickly raised concerns about the privacy of United’s training sessions.

After backlash from fans over the breach of privacy, the video was removed on Friday morning, with the operator issuing an apology for filming the session.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He said: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”.

The operator apologized directly to the club, its latest head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”.

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel stated after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss.

Industry observers note that 'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

In a recent development, 'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'.

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester City could lose an experienced midfielder on a free transfer at the end of the season, with fresh reports suggesting that the player has already identified the European leagues in which he would prefer to continue his career.
  • Mateo Kovacic is expected to leave the Etihad Stadium when his contract expires in June 2027, according to transfer journalist Matteo Moretto, who has also provided an upgrade on the Croatia international's preferred destinations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 20:47.

Manchester City could lose an experienced midfielder on a free transfer at the end of the season, with fresh reports suggesting that the player has already identified the European leagues in which he would prefer to continue his career.

Mateo Kovacic is expected to leave the Etihad Stadium when his contract expires in June 2027, according to transfer journalist Matteo Moretto, who has also provided an upgrade on the Croatia international's preferred destinations.

Speaking to Marca, Moretto claimed that the 32-year-old would welcome a return to Spain or Italy, where he previously represented Real Madrid and Inter Milan respectively.

"He will leave City at the end of the season," Moretto noted, before explaining that Kovacic "would like to return to Spain or Italy", although his salary expectations could influence his options.

The update comes as Kovacic struggles to secure regular playing time under Enzo Maresca, having fallen down the midfield pecking order since the Italian replaced Pep Guardiola.

While City have not officially declared his departure, the midfielder is approaching the final seven months of his contract without a reported agreement over an extension.

Kovacic joined Manchester City from Chelsea in June 2023, signing a four-year contract in a deal worth an initial £25m, with a further £5m potentially payable in add-ons.

The Croatia international was recruited to provide experience, technical quality and composure in midfield, having previously enjoyed considerable success with both Real Madrid and Chelsea.

However, injuries have increasingly disrupted his time in Manchester.

The midfielder was restricted to just nine appearances during the 2025-26 campaign after undergoing surgery to address a troublesome heel problem.

Although he has returned to action this season, his opportunities have remained limited under Maresca.

Kovacic has made eight appearances across all competitions, contributing one goal and one assist, but only one of those outings has been a Premier League start.

He has also been used sparingly in the Champions League, with the manager preferring other midfield options for the majority of City's European fixtures.

His two full appearances in the EFL Cup underline the change in his status, although he was entrusted with the captain's armband in one of those matches.

The situation represents a considerable shift for a player who has won four Champions League titles and previously played an notable role in some of Europe's most successful teams.

Reports linking Kovacic with an exit have circulated for several months.

In September, the Croatian was reportedly considering a January departure after becoming frustrated with his lack of opportunities.

Moretto's latest information, however, points towards a summer move when Kovacic would become available without a transfer fee.

From January, the midfielder will be eligible to negotiate a pre-contract agreement with clubs outside England, potentially allowing him to arrange his next destination before the end of the campaign.

Kovacic's reported preference for Spain or Italy would represent a return to familiar surroundings rather than an entirely newly introduced challenge.

The midfielder spent two seasons with Inter Milan before joining Real Madrid in 2015, where he won three consecutive Champions League titles between 2016 and 2018.

He subsequently moved to Chelsea, initially on loan, and spent five seasons at Stamford Bridge before completing his switch to City.

His experience in Serie A has already attracted attention from Italian clubs.

Juventus were linked with a move for Kovacic in September, when reports suggested that the Turin giants had identified him as one of several potential free-agent signings for the summer of 2027.

The Bianconeri were also said to be monitoring Fikayo Tomori and David Raum as part of their efforts to strengthen the squad without paying substantial transfer fees.

AC Milan have separately been mentioned among Kovacic's possible suitors, although there is no indication that either Italian club has reached an agreement with the player.

The possibility of returning to La Liga also remains open, but Moretto's comments did not identify a Spanish club right now negotiating for his signature.

His wages could prove the biggest obstacle to a move.

Despite the prospect of securing an accomplished international without paying City a transfer fee, interested clubs would still need to reach an agreement over a salary package acceptable to Kovacic.

For City, the latest enhancement raises the prospect of losing another member of Guardiola's former midfield without receiving a transfer fee.

Maresca's current selection decisions suggest that Kovacic is no longer regarded as an automatic starter, although the Croatian remains part of the squad and has not publicly confirmed any intends to leave.

With his contract due to expire next June, the coming months could determine whether he completes his final season in Manchester or attracts an offer to bring forward his departure.

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

“Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”.

Manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a substantial reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in key matches.

“A recurring glitch with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of big trophies.”.

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in substantial games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

“Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”.

In a recent development, pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

It has been revealed that the Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

  • The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

Sources indicate that the departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not at the moment planning to recruit a replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 21:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:04.

Eyeing up a place in the top four of the Premier League, in-form Bournemouth welcome Nottingham Forest to the Vitality Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The spoils were shared in the last meeting between these two teams in May, with an opener from Forest star Morgan Gibbs-White cancelled out in the second half by Cherries attacker Marcus Tavernier to rescue a 1-1 draw.

Bournemouth’s 2026-27 campaign started with just two wins in eight matches across all competitions (D3 L3), including no victories in six Premier League fixtures, but the Cherries have since put together an impressive eight-game winning streak under new boss Marco Rose.

A slender 2-1 success at Ipswich Town prior to the international break helped them climb up to seventh in the Premier League table, just three points behind Liverpool in fourth, and they are now aiming to win five straight top-flight games for the first time in their history.

Since the start of October, Bournemouth have scored more goals across all competitions than any other Premier League team (22), netting at least two goals in each game during their eight-match winning run.

In-form striker Evanilson has been Bournemouth's driving force, with the Brazilian’s goal against Ipswich making him the first Cherries player to score in five successive PL matches. He also has the joint-most top-flight goal involvements this season (nine - five goals, four assists), level with Erling Haaland (nine goals).

Not only do Bournemouth enter Saturday’s contest having never lost in eight previous Premier League battles with Nottingham Forest (W4 D4), but Rose has also won his last four meetings with teams managed by Oliver Glasner (all in the Bundesliga between 2021 and 2023).

After enduring a sluggish start to life under Glasner, winning just one of their first nine Premier League games, Nottingham Forest entered the international break on a massive high after securing a statement 3-1 victory over Manchester City at the City Ground – their first home league win of the campaign.

Liam Delap ended a five-game goal drought with a superb brace against his former club that followed an earlier opener from Jair Cunha, with Forest scoring more goals in this match (three) than they had in their previous six home league fixtures combined (two).

Sitting 16th in the Premier League table and one point above the drop zone, Forest must now translate that momentum onto their travels, having failed to keep an away clean sheet in the top flight since April while losing their last two games on the road against Crystal Palace (3-1) and Brentford (2-0).

Although Forest have scored the second-fewest goals in the division this term (nine), Glasner – who takes charge of his 100th Premier League match on Saturday – will hope that his team’s clinical display against Man City signals a turning point after weeks of frustration in front of goal.

The Tricky Trees head to the Vitality Stadium seeking to win back-to-back league games for only the second time this calendar year, but they are winless in six away league encounters against Bournemouth (D2 L4).

Bournemouth form (all competitions):.

Nottingham Forest Premier League form:.

Bournemouth duo Alex Toth (thigh) and Juanlu Sanchez (ankle) remain sidelined with injuries, while Julian Araujo is still nursing a thigh problem and is unlikely to be involved this weekend.

Rayan sustained a knock on international duty with Brazil, but the winger should be fit to start on the right side of attack, linking up with Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier and red-hot centre-forward Evanilson.

Eli Junior Kroupi is another attacking option pushing to start having made a full recovery from injury and scoring his first goal for France last weekend, while in-demand midfielder Alex Scott is available to start for the first time since suffering a thigh injury with England in October.

As for Nottingham Forest, Nicolas Dominguez (hamstring) remains a long-term absentee and has been joined in the treatment room by Callum Hudson-Odoi (groin), while Neco Williams (ankle) and Xaver Schlager (thigh) have both emerged as doubts after picking up injuries with Wales and Austria respectably over the international break.

Nicolo Savona is yet to play for Forest this season due to a knee injury, but he is back training and may be in a position to return to the matchday squad. A start is seemingly unlikely, though, with Daniel Munoz and either Williams - if fit - or Luca Netz expected to start as wing-backs.

Delap is bidding to score in successive PL games for the first time since April 2025 with Ipswich and is expected to lead the line once again, with Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye potentially providing support in advanced positions; the latter’s inclusion would allow James McAtee to move back into a deeper midfield position.

Bournemouth possible starting lineup:.

Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Cook; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson.

Nottingham Forest possible starting lineup:.

Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams; Ndoye, Gibbs-White; Delap.

Both Bournemouth and Forest enter this contest in buoyant mood as they look to build on positive results prior to the international break.

Although six of Forest's last seven Premier League away games have seen both teams score, we are backing the Cherries to frustrate an opponent they have historically enjoyed facing and secure three more points without reply to extend their impressive winning run to nine matches.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There will be no live UK television coverage of Chelsea’s return to Premier League action against Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.

Xabi Alonso’s side host the Cherries at Stamford Bridge in a traditional 3pm kick-off, with the fixture falling within the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

That means supporters unable to attend will need to follow the match through other channels, rather than watching it live on Sky Sports or TNT Sports.

Although the game will not be televised live in the UK, supporters can follow developments through the official Chelsea website and the Premier League website.

The Saturday 3pm blackout prevents live domestic television broadcasts during the restricted period, although overseas coverage may be available through broadcasters holding the relevant rights.

Highlights will be available after the match through the usual broadcast and digital channels, subject to their respective release schedules.

Chelsea will then turn their attention to a trip to Everton on Saturday, 17 October, with that fixture scheduled for a 12.30pm kick-off at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

For Alonso, the Bournemouth match provides the immediate opportunity to resume Chelsea’s domestic campaign following the international break.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

According to recent reports, but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that united were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent major players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

In a recent development, the question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s upcoming head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

According to recent reports, maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

According to recent reports, was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

In a recent development, the former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

In a recent development, there was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Industry observers note that phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the concern then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

The red card changed the strategy of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

We have to go home with this injustice.

Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

The Blues had a £64m bid rejected during the summer, but their interest has continued into the new season. According to Matt Law of The Telegraph, Chelsea are at the front of the queue of clubs monitoring the 23-year-old.

Bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

The midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. He impressed during the 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia but was withdrawn after 70 minutes. Subsequent examinations revealed a quadriceps problem, with BBC Sport reporting that he could miss six to eight weeks.

Recent findings suggest that his absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

Sources indicate that chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Sources indicate that suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a new contract.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

Sources indicate that that figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026.

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

Recent findings suggest that 🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3.

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes.

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute.

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Recent findings suggest that owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again.

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 21:02, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 21:05.

Two teams that have enjoyed solid starts to their respective 2026-27 La Liga campaigns will lock horns on Saturday, with Alaves hosting Deportivo La Coruna.

The visitors have been one of the surprise packages of the season thus far following their promotion from the second tier last term.

Alaves boast a record of three wins, four draws and five defeats from their 12 matches in Spain's top flight this season, with 13 points leaving them in 12th spot in the La Liga table.

The Blue and Whites drew 0-0 with Sevilla in their last league match, but they thumped Anaitasuna FT 6-1 in the Copa del Rey last time out to secure a position in round two.

Quique Sanchez Flores's side have not managed to triumph in the league since the start of September, but it has still been a strong start to the campaign given that they were 14th last term, only avoiding relegation by a single point.

Alaves have won 20, lost 18 and drawn 11 of their previous 49 matches against Deportivo, and the last two games between the two sides have ended in victories for the Basque outfit.

The Glorious One recorded a 1-0 win over Deportivo when the two teams last locked horns in Spain's top flight, which came in February 2018.

Deportivo secured promotion back to La Liga courtesy of their second-placed finish in last season's Segunda Division, and it has been a successful return to this level of football.

Antonio Hidalgo's side have a record of three wins, six draws and three defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 15 points leaving them in ninth spot in the division.

The Blue and Whites have won two and drawn one of their last three matches, entering the November international break off the back of a 0-0 with Espanyol.

Deportivo have actually only lost one of their last five games in all competitions, while they have picked up six points from their six away matches in La Liga this season.

Alaves will once again be missing Facundo Garces and Mikel Rodriguez through injury, but the home side are otherwise in strong shape for their clash with Deportivo.

Lucas Boye has been in strong form this season, scoring five times in 11 appearances, and the 30-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be an introduction into the team for Mariano Diaz, who has come up with six goals and five assists in 13 appearances during the current campaign.

As for Deportivo, Bright Ede and Zakaria Eddahchouri are both expected to be unavailable for selection due to injury problems.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has now made two appearances off the bench after recovering from an injury, and the experienced attacker could now come back into the starting XI.

Luisimi Cruz has scored twice in 13 appearances this season and is also expected to feature in the starting side, while there should also be a position for Yeremay Hernandez.

Alaves possible starting lineup:.

Sivera; Tenaglia, Koski, Valentini; Perez, Guevara, Blanco, Ibanez, Yusi; Diaz, Boye.

Deportivo La Coruna possible starting lineup:.

Roman; Altimira, Gimenez, Loureiro, Quagliata; Amatucci, Soriano; Mella, Luismi, Hernandez; Aubameyang.

Only two points separates these two teams in the La Liga table, and we are expecting a close match on Saturday, with the points potentially being shared in a low-scoring draw.

Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.

The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.

Industry observers note that thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad. However, this raises questions as to why some England supporters have turned on the defender after he has continued to perform well for Arsenal.

The answer lies with the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

White left the England World Cup camp in November 2022, returning home due to personal reasons. The FA confirmed that White will not return to the squad and asked that his privacy be respected.

He did not play in the first two group games for England and missed the last group game against Wales due to illness.

There were reports that White had fallen out with assistant manager Steve Holland, but neither the FA nor England management confirmed this was the reason he left.

Gareth Southgate later stated there were no problems between White and Holland and that White had simply withdrawn himself from selection after the tournament.

In a recent development, this meant that White would never play for England again while Southgate was still manager. Some fans were clearly upset by this, as they felt White was shunning his country.

Sources indicate that when White returned under Tuchel in March 2026, he was met with a negative reaction. He was booed by the crowd when he scored his first-ever international goal against Uruguay. White was also booed in the same fashion against Japan.

According to recent reports, he has since explained that supporters might view the situation differently if they knew the full story. However, he has chosen not to reveal the private details behind his departure.

Tuchel has shown little concern about White being affected by the controversy.

The England boss remarked after the win on Thursday that he had not heard any boos and praised White’s qualities, work ethic and desire to play for his country.

He believes White can help England win games and added that he has the backing of the coaching staff.

Arsenal fans will be unsurprised to learn that White is still a valuable asset for Mikel Arteta, offering defensive consistency and being able to play as a right or centre-back.

It has been revealed that the bad press that White is receiving from England fans will not go away any time soon. However, he has not done anything to hurt his reputation at club level. The reasons why he left for the World Cup are personal.

Industry observers note that the main focus for Arsenal will be getting him match fit again. As for the England fans, we shall see.
