Recent findings suggest that the measured dispersion along the corresponding high-symmetry direction exhibits dispersive Eu 5d bands crossing EF (Fig. 3d). The measurement geometry, orbital-character analysis and determination of the high-symmetry points for the a–c cleavage plane are described in Supplementary Figs. 15 and 16. The bands near the \(\overline{\Gamma }\) point are labelled α, β and γ, and the band near the zone boundary is denoted φ, following comparison with the density functional theory (DFT) calculations in Fig. 3e. Differences in the number and precise positions of the calculated and measured bands may arise from the simplified treatment of magnetic structure, calculation parameters such as effective on-site Coulomb interaction U and lattice constant, and many-body effects (Supplementary Note 10).

Over a wider energy range, ARPES reveals the Eu 4f- and Si 3p-derived states (Supplementary Fig. 17). The Eu 4f flat bands, labelled FB1–FB3, lie approximately 1–2 eV below EF and are further identified by resonant ARPES measurements (Supplementary Fig. 18). These states are crossed by dispersive Si 3p bands, consistent with orbital-projected calculations. Their location well below EF is consistent with the localized 4f 7 configuration and large local Eu2+ moment.

According to recent reports, the magnetic transitions are accompanied by a pronounced reconstruction of the near-EF electronic structure. High-resolution laser-ARPES demonstrates that the α, β and γ bands evolve strongly across the conical magnetic, spiral magnetic and paramagnetic phases (Fig. 3f). Their characteristic energies shift by approximately 50 meV between the conical magnetic and spiral magnetic phases, followed by a more pronounced reconstruction at TN1, where the three bands merge upon entering the paramagnetic phase (Supplementary Fig. 19). Tracking their energy positions from energy-distribution curve fits (Fig. 3h–j) shows that this reconstruction follows the temperature evolution of the in-plane magnetic order k1 determined by neutron diffraction (Fig. 2i). The calculations (Fig. 3g) reproduce the main evolution in the spiral magnetic and paramagnetic phases, whereas larger deviations occur in the conical magnetic phase, suggesting that the additional b-axis ferromagnetic component has a comparatively smaller influence on the near-EF electronic structure. Similar evolution of the α, β, γ and φ bands is observed at different photon energies and momentum directions (Supplementary Figs. 20 and 21), indicating a robust magnetism-driven reconstruction of the Eu 5d electronic structure.

We attribute this reconstruction to the strong 5d–4f exchange coupling between the localized Eu 4f moments and itinerant Eu 5d electrons through intra-atomic exchange19,20. This exchange lifts the spin degeneracy and accounts for the large band splitting with a gap of approximately 100 meV (ref. 21). Once the spiral magnetic/conical magnetic order develops, the enlarged magnetic unit cell also imposes a periodic exchange potential that folds the reconstructed 5d bands. This interpretation is consistent with the observed substantial Eu moment22. The Si p bands also show reconstruction across TN1, whereas the Eu 4f bands remain nearly unchanged in energy, although the intensity of FB1 starts to decrease at TN2 (Supplementary Fig. 22).

Recent findings suggest that the dominant effect of the a–c-plane magnetic moments is further reflected in the reconstructed electronic structure across multiple momentum planes, arising from the combined effects of exchange splitting and magnetic-zone folding. Consistent reconstruction is observed by ARPES on both the cleaved b–c (100) and a–b (001) surfaces (Supplementary Note 8).

We probe the predicted p-wave symmetry using spin-resolved ARPES on the a–c cleavage plane at 40 K. The relevant symmetry relations predict opposite Sy polarization under \({k}_{y}\to -{k}_{y}\), \(E(0,{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})\,=\) \(E(0,-{k}_{y},{k}_{z},-{S}_{y})\) and unchanged Sy under the corresponding \({k}_{x}\to -{k}_{x}\), \(E({k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})=E(-{k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})\) operation. By varying the photon energy, we sample a series of ky values across successive magnetic Brillouin zones (Fig. 4a,b; additional measurements from an independent facility are shown in Supplementary Fig. 34). At \(({k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z})\,=\) \((0,0.3\times 2{\rm{\pi }}/b,0)\) (cut 1 in Fig. 4d; b is the magnetic-supercell lattice constant), the spectral features associated with the δ, α and γ regions show negative, positive and negative Sy polarization of approximately 5%, respectively. At the corresponding negative-ky position (cut 4 in Fig. 4d; see Supplementary Note 9 for the band assignment), the extracted polarizations show the opposite signs. For intermediate ky values approaching the nodal plane ky ≈ 0, (also −0.5 × 2π/b) the net Sy polarization is strongly suppressed (cuts 2 and 3 in Fig. 4d), consistent with the node-like behaviour expected for an odd-parity spin texture.

These observations are consistent with the predicted spin symmetry but do not establish an eigenstate-resolved test because the measured features contain unresolved band contributions with momentum-dependent spectral weights.

To examine the momentum dependence more systematically, we extract the energy-integrated Sy polarization of the feature labelled α within the fitting-defined integration window at photon energies from 13 eV to 23 eV, sampling successive magnetic Brillouin zones. The extracted polarization exhibits a sign-changing modulation and is strongly suppressed near the ky = 0 nodal regions (Supplementary Fig. 33 and Supplementary Note 9). Despite the finite out-of-plane momentum resolution, the observed modulation is consistent with the odd-ky spin texture expected for p-wave magnetism and with the calculated spin-polarization patterns in both the lattice and magnetic Brillouin zones (Fig. 4b,c and Supplementary Figs. 35 and 36). The variation in modulation amplitude across successive zones is also consistent with momentum-dependent unfolded spectral weights, which redistribute contributions from folded magnetic-supercell states at different extended-zone momenta (Fig. 4b and Supplementary Fig. 36). The persistence of the same sign-reversal pattern in calculations with and without SOC (Fig. 4c) further indicates that the dominant spin texture originates from magnetic symmetry rather than SOC.

In a recent development, in addition, we find that the Sy polarization of the spectral features associated with the δ, α and γ regions remains unchanged within statistical uncertainty for symmetry-related points (kx, ky) and (−kx, ky), consistent with \(E({k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})=E(-{k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z},{S}_{y})\) (Fig. 4e).

Sources indicate that we note two limitations of the spin-ARPES analysis. First, the measured polarization is small, approximately 5%, compared with the calculated maximum contrast of about 25% (Fig. 4c), and the clearest spin-resolved features occur at finite binding energies within the near-EF electronic structure rather than at EF. The measured spin polarization may be reduced by finite energy and momentum resolution and by partial cancellation between unresolved contributions with opposite spin polarizations. Averaging over oppositely chiral magnetic domains could further reduce the signal if such domains are sampled within the illuminated area. Second, the near-EF features contain contributions from multiple folded bands with momentum-dependent spectral weights, and the cuts at positive and negative reduced ky were acquired using different photon energies and sample different extended-zone momenta, so the relative spectral weights contributing to a measured feature may differ. The measurements therefore do not constitute a one-to-one, eigenstate-resolved test of the calculated symmetry relations. In particular, the present data do not uniquely separate the momentum dependence of individual-band spin polarization from changes in the relative spectral weights of unresolved components. Within these limitations, the sign-changing Sy modulation and its suppression near the predicted nodal regions provide spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence consistent with the predicted odd-parity p-wave spin texture of the reconstructed near-EF electronic structure of EuSi.

The large local magnetic moment and its strong coupling with the electronic structure enable the measurement of the magnetic domains with different chiralities using complementary probes23,24. Figure 5a indicates the magnetic domains on the a–c plane measured by MFM in the conical magnetic phase, revealing a bubble-in-stripe pattern with a characteristic width of approximately 10 μm, corresponding to opposite spiral configurations. Similar stripe-like magnetic domains are observed by circularly polarized micro-ARPES with a submicrometre beam spot (Fig. 5b).

Sources indicate that figure 5c,d shows the band dispersions along the \(\overline{\Gamma }-\overline{{\rm{Z}}}\) direction measured in domains A and B using right-handed and left-handed polarized light. Under circularly right-polarized illumination, FB1 and FB3 exhibit stronger spectral weight than FB2 in one domain and weaker spectral weight in the other, generating a clear domain contrast (Fig. 5c). Reversing the light polarization from circularly right-polarized to circularly left-polarized reverses this contrast, producing opposite circular-dichroism signals in domains A and B (Fig. 5e). The circular dichroism is associated with the orbital angular momentum of the Eu 4f bands with b-axis net moment25,26 (Fig. 5f and Supplementary Note 11). The calculated orbital angular momentum reverses between opposite magnetic chiralities, consistent with the observed reversal of the circular-dichroism signal. Thus, the micro-ARPES measurements reveal domains with opposite magnetic chirality and opposite b-axis moment.

The temperature-dependent spatial maps in Fig. 5g show that the domain contrast persists in the conical magnetic phase, weakens in the spiral magnetic phase above TN2 and disappears in the paramagnetic phase. In contrast, MFM no longer resolves the domains in the spiral magnetic phase because of the absence of a net magnetic moment detectable by this probe. The remaining circular-dichroism contrast in the spiral magnetic phase may originate from domains with different chirality, although its microscopic origin requires further scrutiny. Overall, the domain-dependent circular-dichroism demonstrates the coupling between magnetic chirality and the electronic structure. Reversing the magnetic chirality therefore reverses the circular-dichroism response of the electronic states, providing a means to probe the chirality-dependent electronic structure associated with the p-wave magnetic state.

In a recent development, we now discuss the similarities and differences between p-wave magnetic spin splitting and the previously studied f-wave11 spin splitting in transition-metal dichalcogenides. Previous theoretical and experimental studies have demonstrated that in monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (for example, MoS2), SOC induces odd-parity spin splitting in the valence bands27,28,29. Because this splitting is of relativistic origin in a non-magnetic crystal, it is relatively weak and cannot be easily tuned30. By contrast, first-principles calculations predict p-wave spin splitting in EuSi arising predominantly from non-relativistic exchange, whereas ARPES reveals a substantial magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure (Supplementary Table 6). Because this p-wave state originates from the chiral magnetic order, the calculated dependence of the spin texture on magnetic chirality suggests a possible route to controlling the associated spin polarization.

Industry observers note that compared with previously discussed ‘p-wave’ magnetic candidates8,9, EuSi provides a particularly clean realization of the archetypal p-wave symmetry setting8. In the spiral phase, the refined magnetic structure of stoichiometric EuSi preserves the combined \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) symmetry and has zero net magnetization, providing the symmetry setting for the predicted odd-parity p-wave spin texture without complications from finite magnetization. This combination has not been achieved in earlier candidate materials such as NiI2 or Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12. In NiI2, \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) symmetry is broken by the incommensurate non-collinear spin structure8, whereas in Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12 a weak magnetization breaks time-reversal symmetry and generates a large anomalous Hall effect9.

Furthermore, EuSi serves as an advantageous material platform because of its stoichiometric and metallic nature, and a relatively high temperature window (33.4–62 K) compared with those of low-ordering-temperature metallic counterparts such as CeNiAsO and Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12 (approximately 8 K; see Supplementary Table 7 for detailed comparison). Taken together, these attributes position EuSi as a particularly promising material platform for exploring and ultimately harnessing p-wave magnetism in electronic structures.

Metallic p-wave magnets are predicted to host unconventional responses, including field-free spin-polarized transport, a large non-relativistic Edelstein effect10 and non-relativistic Ising superconductivity11. When the spiral order is canted and forms a conical state, an unconventional and large anomalous Hall effect can be observed. Analogous effects, such as the magneto-optical Kerr effect, are expected to be pronounced as well. Through combined theoretical and experimental approaches, our results provide evidence for p-wave magnetism in the electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, associated with its chiral magnetic order and combined time-reversal and lattice-translation symmetry in the spiral phase (33.4–62 K). EuSi therefore provides a realistic and accessible platform for investigating symmetry-protected transport and optical responses driven by magnetism. Beyond fundamental interest, the controllability of its metallic and chiral magnetic states may enable field-free spintronic functionalities and pave the way towards engineering p-wave-correlated and topological electronic phases in itinerant systems.

It has been revealed that euSi single crystals were grown using the Bridgman method with an Eu:Si elemental ratio of 1:1. Eu (99.95% purity) and Si (99.99% purity) were mixed and placed in a tantalum crucible. The crucible was sealed in vacuum. The sealed tube was heated to 1,450 °C for over 12 h and maintained at that temperature for 24 h. The solution was then slowly cooled to room temperature. Owing to the sensitivity of the investigated phase to oxygen and moisture, the specimen used for the single-crystal diffraction experiment was prepared (mounted) in a protective atmosphere (an argon-filled glovebox). The single crystal used for this experiment was mechanically detached (cut) from the grown single crystal and mounted in a glass capillary (0.2 mm diameter) to prevent reaction with air and moisture during the data collection. Details regarding data collection and the refinement of the crystal structure are listed in the Supplementary Tables 1–3. Low-temperature X-ray powder diffraction was carried out at beamline ID22 of the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF). For this purpose, a portion of the grown single crystal was powdered, sieved through a 32-µm sieve and placed into a 0.3-mm glass capillary. The data were collected at specific temperatures using a helium-cooled cryostat and a multi-analyser stage for recording of the diffraction pattern. At temperatures below 45 K, the intensity of the beam was reduced using an attenuator to prevent the sample from heating up. The results of the low-temperature X-ray powder diffraction are shown in Supplementary Fig. 4.

In a recent development, X-ray absorption spectroscopy and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism measurements were performed at the high-field magnet endstation of beamline I10 at Diamond Light Source, UK, with a base temperature of 5 K and magnetic field up to ±14 T along the direction of the incident beam. The crystals were cleaved in situ along the a–c (010) plane under ultrahigh vacuum, and the angle between the incident beam and the crystal (010) plane was kept at either 0° (normal incidence) or 70° (grazing incidence). X-ray absorption spectroscopy was carried out in total-electron-yield mode at the Eu M4,5 edges. X-ray magnetic circular-dichroism spectra were obtained by subtracting the absorption spectra measured with opposite helicities of the incident X-ray beam, which was aligned either parallel or antiparallel to the applied magnetic field.

High-resolution ARPES measurements were performed at beamlines BL5-2 of the Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource (SSRL), A-branch of the Bloch beamline at MAX IV, and BL03U of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility (SSRF). At BL5-2, a Scienta Omicron DFS30 analyser was used, achieving an overall energy and angular resolution of 20 meV and 0.2°. At Bloch and BL03U, a Scienta Omicron DA30L analyser was used, achieving an overall energy and angular resolution of 20 meV and 0.2°. High-resolution laser-based ARPES measurements were performed on home-built set-up (hν = 6.994 eV) at ShanghaiTech University. Data were collected using an electron analyser (DA30L Scienta Omicron). The total convolved energy and angle resolution were 5 meV and 0.1°, respectively. Micro-ARPES measurements were performed at BL07U of SSRF. The beam with photon energy from 88 eV to 102 eV was focused using a Fresnel zone plate and a spatial resolution of approximately 400 nm was achieved. The data were collected by a hemispherical Scienta Omicron DA30L electron analyser. The instrument energy and momentum resolution were approximately 15 meV and 0.01 Å−1, respectively. In all set-ups, the samples were cleaved in situ at approximately 10 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 5 × 10−11 torr.

The spin-resolved ARPES experiments were performed using a Scienta DA30L analyser integrated with a very-low-energy-diffraction spin detector at the National Synchrotron Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) BL13U. The samples were cleaved in situ at approximately 40 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 2 × 10−10 torr. For these experiments, an effective Sherman function of 0.25 was used. Spin-resolved ARPES measurements at the U125-PGM beamline of BESSY II were performed using the spin-ARPES endstation equipped with a Scienta R4000 analyser coupled to two Mott-type spin detectors. The samples were also cleaved in situ at approximately 50 K and measured under ultrahigh vacuum below 2 × 10−10 torr. For these experiments, an effective Sherman function of 0.16 was adopted. The spin polarization was determined from \(\mathrm{Polarization}=(1/{S}_{\mathrm{eff}})\times ({I}_{\mathrm{up}}-{I}_{\mathrm{down}})/({I}_{\mathrm{up}}+{I}_{\mathrm{down}})\), in which Iup and Idown are the measured photoelectron intensities in the two spin channels and Seff is the effective Sherman function.

Industry observers note that the statistical uncertainties were estimated from the counting statistics of the two spin-detector channels. Assuming independent Poisson statistics, the measured counts Iup and Idown have standard deviations \({\sigma }_{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}}=\sqrt{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}}\) and \({\sigma }_{{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}=\sqrt{{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}\), respectively. Standard error propagation gives \({\sigma }_{{S}_{y}}=\frac{2}{{S}_{\mathrm{eff}}}\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{\mathrm{up}}{I}_{\mathrm{down}}}{{({I}_{\mathrm{up}}+{I}_{\mathrm{down}})}^{3}}}\). For energy-dependent polarization curves, this expression was applied separately to each energy bin; for the integrated polarization of a spectral feature, Iup and Idown represent the total counts accumulated within the corresponding energy-integration window. All shaded uncertainty envelopes and error bars in the spin-ARPES figures denote one standard deviation.

Industry observers note that neutron-diffraction experiments were conducted at the HB-3A DEMAND in the High-Flux Isotope Reactor at Oak Ridge National Lab. A piece of a EuSi single crystal with dimensions of approximately 4 × 3 × 0.1 mm3 was aligned in the (0KL) scattering plane and cooled. The wavelength used was 1.541 Å. The data were reduced using MANTID31 and ReTIA32. Symmetry analysis was performed using SARAh33, and magnetic-structure refinement was performed using FullProf34,35.

Sources indicate that the first-principles calculations of the band structures and Fermi surface were performed by using the first-principles DFT methods implemented in the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP)36,37. The exchange-correlation and the ion-electron interactions are treated by the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional38 and the projector augmented-wave method39,40 under the generalized gradient approximation. Throughout all calculations, the convergence criteria for energy are less than 2 × 10−5 eV, and the plane-wave energy cut-off is set to 400 eV. The k-point sampling uses a Monkhorst–Pack scheme41 with an accuracy of 0.02π Å−1 for self-consistent electronic calculations. To correctly describe the strong correlation effects of the Eu f orbitals, the on-site Coulomb interaction was treated using an effective Hubbard U of 5 eV.

It has been revealed that for electrical-transport measurements, a single crystal was cut into a bar shape. A standard six-probe method was used for longitudinal resistivity and transverse Hall measurements. Electrical-transport data were collected using a physical-property measurement system (PPMS; Quantum Design). Magnetic-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements were performed using a magnetic property measurement system (MPMS; Quantum Design) and PPMS. Thermal-expansion measurements were conducted in the PPMS using a homemade capacitive dilatometer.

The MFM experiments were performed with a homemade helium-3 atomic force microscopy system using commercial piezoresistive cantilevers (spring constant k ≈ 3 N m−1 and resonant frequency approximately 43 kHz). The tips were coated with a nominally 100-nm-thick cobalt layer by magnetron sputtering. The MFM data were acquired by Nanonis SPM Controllers (SPECS) with a phase-locked loop. The MFM signal, the resonant frequency shift of the cantilever, is proportional to the out-of-plane stray field gradient generated by the sample. By using the constant-height mode, MFM images are acquired on a scanning plane approximately 200 nm above the surface.

First-principles calculations were performed with the commercial VASP package. The custom code used in this study, including the scripts for unfolding the spin-resolved magnetic-supercell electronic structure, is available via Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23172154 (ref. 42).

E.C. and C.F. initiated the project. E.C., C.F. and Zhongkai Liu conceived of and designed the experiments. E.C. grew the single crystal, conducted magnetization and electrical-transport measurements, and analysed the data. M.Y. and E.C. conducted preliminary ARPES experiments, and observed large band splitting. Y.H. conducted the neutron-diffraction experiments and analysed the data. Zhongkai Liu proposed the possible existence of p-wave magnetism in EuSi, and Junwei Liu and Y.G. confirmed the chiral p-wave magnetism in theory based on symmetry analysis and DFT calculations. Y.Y., Jieyi Liu, H.C., Y.C., G.v.d.L. and Zhongkai Liu performed X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray magnetic circular dichroism and ARPES experiments and analysis. Y.G., J.P., J.Z., J.A., Junwei Liu and L.Š. performed symmetry analysis and DFT calculations. Y.-T.C. and W.W. performed the MFM measurements. Z. Lu and H.W. performed the orbital angular momentum calculations. Y.P., U.B., V.H., R.K., W.S., P.B., M.H., D.L., X.S., L.N. and J.O. helped with data collection. B.H.G. performed scanning transmission electron microscopy measurements. R.L., A.F., J.S.-B., O.R., Zhanfeng Liu and S.C. assisted with spin-ARPES data collection. E.C., Y.H., L.Š., Junwei Liu, Zhongkai Liu and C.F. supervised this study. Zhongkai Liu, E.C., Junwei Liu and L.Š. wrote the paper with input from all authors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 08:12, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:14.

Manchester City and Fulham will continue their respective Premier League campaigns with a contest at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts are third in the Premier League table, six points behind the leaders Arsenal, while Fulham are down in 15th spot in the division on 10 points.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 12.30pm UK time on Saturday.

The Premier League match between Man City and Fulham will be played at the Etihad Stadium.

The corresponding game last season ended in a 3-0 win for the Citizens, while Fulham have not beaten Man City in any competition since a league clash in April 2009.

The Premier League match will be shown live on TNT Sports 1.

TNT Sports is also available as an add-on for Amazon's Prime Video app.

Goals will be posted on the FootballOnTNT X account, while highlights will also be uploaded to the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel after the match.

Meanwhile, on Saturday, BBC One's Match of the Day programme will begin at 10.20pm and run until 11.45pm, with highlights of the match also available via that avenue.

Man City have lost each of their last three Premier League matches to Aston Villa, Brighton & Hove Albion and Nottingham Forest, which has seen them lose vital ground in the title race.

Enzo Maresca's side must bounce back on Saturday to avoid the possibility of Arsenal pulling further clear at the summit, as the Gunners could prove incredibly difficult to catch.

Man City have won each of their last 20 matches against Fulham in all competitions - a remarkable run - but their last three losses to the London club have come on home soil.

Fulham are unbeaten in their last four Premier League matches, and they picked up a point in a 1-1 draw with Aston Villa in their last away league fixture.

Man City dare not suffer another defeat or it could spell serious trouble for their title ambitions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Lamine Yamal mercilessly taunted England rival Elliot Anderson as tensions flared during the Three Lions’ spectacular victory over Spain on Sunday night.
  • England held on for a memorable 3-2 victory in Madrid after Anderson was given his marching orders with just under 30 minutes remaining.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 06:21 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 14:24 EST, 16 November 2026.

Lamine Yamal mercilessly taunted England rival Elliot Anderson as tensions flared during the Three Lions’ spectacular victory over Spain on Sunday night.

England held on for a memorable 3-2 victory in Madrid after Anderson was given his marching orders with just under 30 minutes remaining.

Thomas Tuchel’s side were three goals in front and cruising when Anderson - looking to atone for a sloppy error from Jarrel Quansah - cynically hauled down 19-year-old Yamal as he barrelled down on goal.

Spain were awarded a penalty for the infringement, and Anderson was sent off - much to the Manchester City star’s bemusement.

According to recent reports, but Yamal, aggrieved by Anderson’s challenge, made a beeline for the midfielder following the challenge. According to Spanish reports, the attacker mouthed ‘tonto, tonto’ to his rival following his dismissal.

The colloquial term can mean a number of things, varying from idiot, fool or stupid, but in any case is far from a term of affection.

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨بطاقة حمراء لإليوت أندرسون ولامين يامال يستفزه🤯🤯#اسبانيا_انجلترا #دوري_الأمم_الأوروبية pic.twitter.com/cOrswp5kCC.

Lamine Yamal was spotted taunting Elliot Anderson after the Manchester City midfielder was sent off for a challenge on the winger.

The moment came in England's historic 3-2 win over the World Champions.

Anderson blanked the 19-year-old while a VAR review confirmed the on-field official’s decision was the right one, eventually trudging off the pitch.

A fired-up Yamal galvanised the reigning world champions as they searched for an unlikely comeback.

Mikel Oyarzabal, the man who scored Spain’s winner against England two years ago in the 2024 Euros final, converted the spot kick before Nico Williams scored Spain’s second after latching on to an excellent Yamal cross.

However, Las Rojas fell short, with Sunday’s defeat their first in an imperious 43-game run.

A jubilant Thomas Tuchel hailed the match as his ‘best performance of my time as manager’.

It has been revealed that ‘What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,’ Tuchel remarked after the game. ’Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

‘It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.’.

AC Milan and Juventus are both keeping tabs on Benjamin Sesko’s situation at Manchester United, according to a report.

According to recent reports, united paid around €80m to sign Sesko from RB Leipzig, hoping he would be the long-term fix for the No.9 position. Last season he performed reasonably well, scoring 11 goals in 30 Premier League games which was not bad for a 22-year-old in a latest league.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that this season, however, he is stuck on one goal in four league games, having spent time out injured too. With massive changes at Old Trafford – including the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as the head coach – it is another blank slate for the squad.

It has been revealed that for example, club captain Bruno Fernandes has been linked with a move to Milan. Now, according to journalist Alessandro Jacobone, a new idea has emerged for the centre-forward position, perhaps if the pursuit of Nicolo Tresoldi does not go to initiative.

“Juve and Milan are keeping an eye on things. But summer is the most realistic scenario. Benjamin Šeško could leave Manchester United, with Juventus and Milan having already made some preliminary enquiries to assess the financial feasibility of a potential move,” he remarked.

It has been revealed that “For now, these are only preliminary discussions, useful for finding out the figures, conditions and possible deal structures. No concrete negotiations have been initiated.

Industry observers note that “Sources close to the player’s camp are also playing down the possibility of a transfer as early as January, making a potential move in the next summer window considerably more likely. One to watch.”.

Industry observers note that four of those 11 goals in his debut campaign came off the bench too as he developed a knack for being an impact substitute. This could give Milan food for thought, given they are looking for an alter-ego to Goncalo Ramos rather than someone to solely take over the striker role.

Arsenal and Norway captain Martin Odegaard has undoubtedly spoken to Antonio Nusa about a potential move to North London.

That is according to experienced former Aston Villa, Everton and Tottenham scout and expert on Norwegian football, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The Gunners are thought to be leading the race to sign the 21-year-old, who has burst onto the transfer wish lists of several European giants this season.

Nusa had already been recognised as a strong talent but he has taken a step up at RB Leipzig this season and has already set his own career-record tallies for both goals and assists in a single campaign after just 15 games.

The winger is under contract until 2029 and is expected to leave the German side in the coming months, but it remains to be seen if a move will take place in January.

Leipzig have reportedly been intent on keeping the Norway international until the summer, but an offer the right size may well change that stance.

Industry observers note that on paper, Nusa is a no-brainer of a signing for Arsenal. He is a left-sided winger, which Mikel Arteta's team desperately needs, and he has the pace that they seem to lack.

And after a summer window that saw the Gunners miss out on several top targets for that position, there is growing demand to strengthen Arteta's options.

"If it's the time to sell and the way the boy's playing, you're going to get £80million for him," King told Football Insider.

"To be honest, you look at the crazy figures they're talking about Yamal at Barcelona. I mean, this kid isn't far off him. He's got the Arsenal captain [Odegaard], who's his captain in the national team.

"I can't imagine that they haven't had a little chat about the Emirates [Stadium], or what's it like in London, or whatever.".

Although Odegaard largely features on the right of the Arsenal midfield, he is given the licence to roam where ever the game needs him.

And should Nusa arrive and be deployed on the left, Arteta will be sure to get the pair combining as much as possible.

The pair have demonstrated on several occasions that they have a excellent understanding of each other, and could be a deadly combination to exploit.

And off the pitch, there is no doubting that a presence like Odegaard's will certainly make what will likely be a tough transition easier for Nusa.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Gomez could find himself in a tricky position next summer as he edges closer to a move away from Liverpool.

The 29-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season, and there is a growing expectation that his terms will not be renewed, and he could leave the club for free.

So far this season, the defender has started just three games, and is unlikely to play a massive role in Andoni Iraola's looks despite his continued involvement in squads.

However, former Man United chief scout Mick Brown warned Football Insider that there may be a lack of suitors for Gomez next summer, even on a free transfer.

The defender is likely to command significant wages to move on a free, while there are lingering concerns about his fitness and the fact he has never established himself at Liverpool.

After what will be 12 years at Liverpool come the end of the season, Gomez could struggle to find a newly introduced club, as they share the Reds' doubts over his reliability.

Brown told Football Insider on 18 November that Gomez is edging closer to a move away from Liverpool with no plans in place to agree a contract extension as things stand.

The situation is still up in the air, and there have been suggestions that the versatile defender would be willing to stay if he was offered the opportunity to pen a new deal.

However, with the growing expectation that he will move on a free transfer, questions have been asked about which clubs will be prepared to take the gamble.

"The problem for Joe Gomez is, there isn't a long line of clubs queuing up to sign him," Brown told Football Insider.

"So he could be left in no-man's-land if he leaves Liverpool on a free transfer, because then it's about whether any clubs are prepared to take a gamble on him.

"His fitness and injury record is going to be a major concern, while there are doubts about the fact he has never managed to establish himself at Liverpool.

"He's been there forever, it feels like, but can you name one time when he's had a real consistent run in the team and looked like he would be an vital player?

"He certainly hasn't done that in recent memory, so obviously that leads to doubts about how good he really is at this stage.

"I'm sure clubs will be keeping an eye on it, they always are when players like that are available for free, but I have my doubts about how many will be willing to make a move.

"I can't imagine he wages will be cheap either, especially on a free transfer, so all of these things have to be taken into consideration.".

Despite doubts about which clubs could be tempted to make a move for Gomez in the summer, he has had a number of long-term suitors keen to lure him away before.

In 2025, the likes of AC Milan, Crystal Palace and Brighton were all linked with the versatile defender, but he ultimately remained at Liverpool despite that interest.

Meanwhile, Football Insider reported during the summer that West Ham have shown an interest in signing Gomez and could be tempted to revisit the deal.

The decision was ultimately made to keep him at Anfield, but that is unlikely to have deterred the Hammers' long-term interest should he leave Liverpool for free.

His availability as a free agent is likely to spark further interest, despite the doubts over his fitness and his level, and the Championship outfit could make a move.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 14:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:35 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • 'It was like meeting a kid at a sixth-form careers day'.
  • When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:35 EST, 16 November 2026.

'It was like meeting a kid at a sixth-form careers day'. That was the verdict, slightly unflattering but endearing all the same, of one Premier League chief after encountering James Trafford.

When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.

It has been revealed that he is the son of a Cumbrian farmer and the Lego was of a tractor, which he would save for later in the tournament. 'You don't want to go too early,' he noted.

Industry observers note that none of this is a criticism. Far from it. There was a boyish charm, an innocence, even, and Trafford was engaging organization. Nonetheless, he did not sound ready for the likes of a World Cup semi-final against Argentina. Thomas Tuchel agreed.

But every boy will one day become a man. On a ferocious and febrile night in Madrid, no place for adolescents, we may just have witnessed James Trafford's graduation ceremony.

Without his double save in stoppage-time, England would have left Spain without a famous, and deserved, victory. One Spanish title labelled it 'la actuacion de su vida', the performance of his life. You wonder how much they saw of his loan spell at Accrington Stanley, but the sentiment stands.

James Trafford celebrates with Jarell Quansah, Dan Burn and Ezri Konsa during his starring performance in Spain.

Trafford pictured with his farmer father, David, in the cab of his tractor with their dogs (Source: James Trafford).

In a recent development, madrid daily AS exclaimed: 'Magisterio de Trafford!' Translated, 'A Trafford Masterclass!'. They claim he was the reason Spain could not complete their comeback, and they would be right.

When Tuchel stood with us in a corridor of the Metropolitano Stadium on the eve of the game, he had no glitch confirming that Trafford would start. His message, though, was clear - it was sink or swim for a goalkeeper who turned 24 last month.

In a recent development, not only did Trafford keep his head above water, it was he who pulled the team ashore. It was he to whom his senior colleagues ran in celebration. Ezri Konsa nearly took the shirt off Trafford's back, such was the force of his gratitude. But maybe this was the occasion when Trafford took the No 1 jersey from the back of Jordan Pickford, the holder for nearly a decade.

Sources indicate that pickford has done nothing wrong. Were Trafford to still display that maturity deficit, Pickford would be a reliable custodian heading to Euro 2028. This is not Peter Shilton post Italia 90, an uncomfortable truth of a great in need of the retirement barn. The 32-year-old has plenty to give on the back of all he has already given.

This, admitted Tuchel after the 3-2 win, is a selection dilemma that allows a manager to sleep well at night.

'There is no headache at all!' he boomed. 'I'm so far away from a headache, I cannot imagine.

Trafford left Manchester City with the strategy to usurp Jordan Pickford as England No 1.

Jude Bellingham certainly seemed impressed with the performance of the goalkeeper.

'This is what we wanted. This is the best thing that can happen to all of us, also to Pickers. It is amazing how they push each other, and if then Traff has a performance like this, he has it because he knows he's well prepared. He gets the push from his colleagues and competitors.'.

Tuchel has seen enough of Trafford in training and around camp to believe he is ready for promotion. He has watched him for Leeds, where he rates as the best performing goalkeeper in the Premier League. His 'net goals prevented' (4.4) and 'save percentage' (81.4) are higher than any rival this season, including Pickford.

'You always have to deserve your place,' added Tuchel. 'You will never get a gift and just get a game (for the sake of it). So he deserved to play and we expected this kind of performance. It was not only the last save, but also the build-up play and not losing focus. He has proved it on this stage, so this gives him a lot of belief. Now, it's on him to keep going for it.'.

According to recent reports, it, you presume, is the No 1 jersey. Trafford has made no secret of his desire to take it from Pickford, and he told us in the summer that such ambition was the motivation behind him wanting to leave Manchester City for a second time.

According to recent reports, that day, he flipped his room key with a magician's sleight of hand throughout the interview, a dexterity useful for Lego. Better still for fingertip saves such as the one to deny Aymeric Laporte in the 91st minute.

In a recent development, also in the gift pack from his girlfriend were two face masks. 'Very thoughtful,' he quipped. But that is another observation, bordering on concern, that some prospective buyers have made in recent years - on the goalkeeping scale of uber professional to joker, he resides too close to the latter. We have seen, even this season, the odd concentration lapse that speaks to that thought.

Trafford has played a starring role in goal since moving to Leeds United in the summer.

Industry observers note that but there was also a feeling that Trafford needed more exposure and responsibility before the penny dropped and his value was realised. Already, £95million has been spent on him in transfer fees.

At Leeds, and now with England, he has been given that stage, as Tuchel calls it. The head coach maintains that Pickford is his first choice, but it was Trafford he picked for both Nations League fixtures against Spain, the ones that really mattered, the ones that would strengthen or threaten his own employment.

As for Trafford's career prospects, to revisit our opening line, England's No 1 sounds like a fair vocation.

Thomas Tuchel wants England to use victory in the Nations League finals as a springboard to winning Euro 2028 at Wembley.

The head coach admits it has taken him a while to recover from the trauma of his side’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July, for which he was heavily criticised.

But after beating world champions Spain 3-2 on Sunday night, topping their Nations League group ahead of March’s quarter-finals and next summer's finals, Tuchel is finally able to look forward with positivity and belief.

‘I saw the celebrations in Portugal when they won the Nations League,’ he remarked. ‘It’s just the best, the best preparation we can have for the Euros. We want to have these matches on the highest level to prove ourselves and to gain confidence, to see where we are and to adjust our game where we need to, that’s what this Nations League is perfect for. We want to win it.’.

England have won five of their six matches since the World Cup, losing only to Spain at Wembley in September. In the build up to that game, Tuchel was involved in heated exchanges with observers who continued to question his tactics in the final half hour against Argentina.

’It took me a while to digest (the World Cup exit) and see the way forward, how we can help and adjust and improve, and how we can do this together,’ he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We had reviews and so on, but clarity then came together with the players. Straight away we had the energy right to take the next steps. The ideas became more clear for me, even if it was not so easy the first week, to overcome and arrive with different emotions. Some were still upset from the World Cup. Some were new in the team. Some had digested it, some had not digested it. But it was notable to have this kind of process together.

Recent findings suggest that ‘(Spain) was a complete performance that makes me very proud. It's a full package of belief, of courage, of commitment, of togetherness, of relying on each other and stepping up in this moment.’.

Tuchel, though, has rejected the idea that seeing out the win Madrid was proof that he has learned from his mistakes in Atlanta.

It has been revealed that ‘Not at all, I think we would not have been in this situation if it was 11 against 11,’ he said. ‘For me, it was Mexico reloaded (not Argentina). It's one man down, but what can you do? It is their strength to have ball possession, to overload and find the gaps. It just plays totally into their hands and it comes wave after wave. It felt like three hours and thirty minutes!’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:00.

England should be seen as the favourites to win the UEFA Nations League ahead of the quarter-final draw, a former Three Lions striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Thomas Tuchel's side will learn their knockout fate on Friday morning when the draw for the last eight is held, and England head into the ceremony as one of the four seeded teams courtesy of finishing first in League A Group 3.

The Three Lions unexpectedly pipped world and European champions Spain to top spot courtesy of an engrossing 3-2 win over La Roja on Sunday, ending an unparalleled 43-game unbeaten run for Luis de la Fuente's side.

England will meet one of Belgium, Netherlands or Norway in the quarter-finals, while France, Portugal and Germany represent the other three Group A winners going for glory.

Despite the strength of the draw, former England striker Mark Hateley believes that Tuchel's men have made themselves the favourites to win the trophy for the first time, and also reserved special praise foe the goalkeeping heroics of James Trafford.

Asked if England are leading the charge for Nations League stardom, Hateley replied: "100%. That's the best I've seen England, or any team, play over a period of, say, 60 minutes.

"They were incredible: high press, press, press, press, going man for man, confident enough to go man for man at the back against the world champions, allowing your midfield players to jump up with the strikers.

Industry observers note that “It was tremendous to watch, the very best we've seen from an England side for many, many years, honestly. It was superb. We went to 3-0, rightly so, and Spain never had a shot. Their first was 50 minutes in, in the second half.

According to recent reports, “Trafford must have thought 'this was a goddamn easy game.' The only time I think he was at fault was his starting position for the penalty, when Anderson brought the boy down. If his starting position had been higher, I think he'd have made the interception. That would be my only fault for the goalkeeper.

“If you’re a shot stopper, you’re a shot stopper - it’s just the other side of his game, where you're reading it and where you should be, playing as that sweeper.

Sources indicate that "With the way we were pressing, the only ball really on for Spain was a ball in behind into the last third, which was empty for long periods. There was nobody there where I thought he could have been. But those are the things you pick up on and learn from.”.

England have only ever competed in the Nations League knockout stages once before in the inaugural 2018-19 edition, when they reached the finals courtesy of beating Spain and Croatia to first place in their group.

However, at a time when the Nations League Finals only comprised four teams, Gareth Southgate's side fell to a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands in the semi-finals, meaning that they are still awaiting their first knockout-phase win in the tournament.

England could only place third in the group stage of the 2020-21 tournament, before an embarrassing relegation to League B in the 2022-23 edition, although they swiftly returned to the top tier.

In the current format, England's record of five wins, one loss and 19 goals scored represented their best-ever performance in the group stage of the Nations League, fuelling the belief that the Three Lions can finally end their trophy drought in 2027.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

It has been revealed that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It has been revealed that it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

Sources indicate that “It was a really good fight,” Alisson mentioned, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

Recent findings suggest that “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Recent findings suggest that don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Recent findings suggest that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Recent findings suggest that alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Industry observers note that “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose said. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

It has been revealed that speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that revealed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

Sources indicate that "Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y.

Recent findings suggest that "That's a substantial moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39.

Industry observers note that cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young noted on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose big players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Fair play to anyone who retained Brobbey in their Fantasy Football teams this week...

Maresca’s side maintain their immaculate record, but boy were they made to work for it this afternoon.

Sunderland are still 5-3 down but have not given up the ghost. Surely the best match of the season so far?

It ends goalless at Elland Road after Mitchell’s goal was disallowed for offside. Kamada went close to breaking the deadlock in the final stages...

Bournemouth lose at the Vitality for the first time in 13 matches as Iraola makes a winning return to the South Coast. Liverpool were hardly impressive, but to their credit they managed the final stages of this match with a minimum of fuss.

Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium with a win! ✅ pic.twitter.com/FSgvE6EGFB.

Bournemouth are awarded a corner but Brooks’ delivery goes straight into the inviting gloves of Alisson.

Koumas pressures Petrovic, but the goalkeeper highlights off some tidy footwork to escape the danger.

Bournemouth cannot get out though, and Petrovic is forced into a routine save off Koumas moments later.

Bournemouth win a free-kick in a dangerous position after a handball, but Scott cannot get his strike up and down fast enough and it sails over.

Four minutes of stoppage time to play.

Haaland gets in on the act, but only after a VAR check. That should be that...

Erling Haaland has now scored against all 25 teams he has faced in the Premier League ✅⚽ pic.twitter.com/X9uqcrgbwk.

Araujo gets his pocket picked in the corner but Jebbison cannot compose himself and blasts his cross off the other side of the pitch.

Liverpool go the other way and win a corner, but Mac Allister puts too much air on his delivery and it is easily dealt with.

In a recent development, rayan wins a free-kick as he holds off Kerkez on the halfway line. Bournemouth then switch play to the far side but Truffert’s speculative effort flies well over the bar.

Nyoni shows off his composure on the ball, playing simple passes on the half-turn to keep play flowing. The midfield area is quite congested, which suits Liverpool at this point in the game.

Industry observers note that liverpool are baiting Bournemouth’s press in an attempt to play around their front line. They are doing a good job at holding on to the ball and frustrating their opponents, for now.

Gravenberch and Koumas are on for Gakpo and Isak.

Brooks has brought some energy to Bournemouth’s forays down the left. He attempts to slip a ball into the left channel but Nyoni is wise to it and positions himself perfectly to cut it out.

In a recent development, liverpool have dropped deep and Bournemouth wait patiently for an opening. They eventually find Tavernier in the left half-space but his cross flies over everyone.

That is his last contribution to the match as Rose rings the changes: Tavernier, Smith and Christie make way for Brooks, Jebbison and Cook.

Truffert spins in a teasing ball from the left but Jacquet does well to flick the ball away from the danger zone.

Wirtz and Barcola make way for Nyoni and Munoz. Quiet afternoon from both of the outgoing players.

A stunning block from Hill prevents Isak pulling trigger as he looked to have the goal in his sights.

Truffert clears the resulting corner to safety.

Isak is concentrating his efforts in more central areas and here he almost gets played in behind but the ball just runs away from him. Better.

Worth mentioning that Jacquet has been fantastic in all phases of the game. Plenty of advanced regains and tidy passes forward.

Recent findings suggest that it’s raining goals in Manchester and no prizes for guessing who has scored for Sunderland. Brobbey has his hat-trick.

Industry observers note that brobbey has his hat-trick and the look on Enzo Maresca’s face as he assesses the defending from his team. They’ve been great pouring forward, less so trying to stymie Sunderand’s attack. But this is one of those games where you just sit back and enjoy the unfolding drama. It’s been so good from both teams.

Semenyo gets his second goal of the afternoon to extend the league leaders’ advantage.

Recent findings suggest that chance! Jacquet jumps and wins the ball well inside Bournemouth’s half and his intervention sends the ball into Isak’s path. The forward just drags his effort wide and turns out he was in an offside postion anyhow.

What an afternoon this is turning out to be. There have been more slices than on an erratic day on the local municipal golf course and Ronald Araujo is the latest to be afflicted by the condition. None of that will matter to Andoni Iraola, though, as Alexander Isak’s fourth goal in four Premier League games has given Liverpool a huge advantage. They haven’t played with fluency but the breakthrough was significant.

It has been revealed that isak opens the scoring at the Vitality, finally getting into the box and sweeping in from close range. So much credit has to go to Gakpo who tiptoes past two Bournemouth defenders by the touchline before spearing a cross infield, and while he may not be attributed with the assist owing to a touch off Wirtz, his delivery makes it all the way through to Isak who taps in.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Adams has been superb as one of Bournemouth’s two midfield sentries. Kerkez looks to have been played into the left channel but the American swoops in and shields the ball out of play before staring down his Hungarian opponent.

In a recent development, liverpool give up possession in Bournemouth’s half and Christie strides forward releasing Rayan before continuing his run to the near post. The Brazilian picks out his team-mate but Christie gets too strong a contact on the ball and the ball sails wide.

Truffert passes the ball straight to Gakpo inside his own box but Adams is on the scene in a flash and snaps into a tackle and takes the ball away from the Liverpool forward.

The second has already settled into a holding pattern, with neither side creating much. Isak makes a run down the right hand side and, with players loaded in the box, he blasts the ball high into the sky and beyond his team-mates. That pretty much sums things up.

It has been revealed that wirtz has given the ball away twice in the first minute of the second half. Carragher is on Sky Sports commentary duties and he claims he’s surprised to see him back out on the pitch.

Szoboszlai concedes a foul on the far side but the subsequent delivery is too heavy and sails over everyone.

No half-time changes from either manager.

Isak’s first-half heatmap makes for interesting reading. The good news, for Liverpool fans, is that he’s stationed himself predominantly in the final third. The bad news... those positions have been everywhere but the box.

There must be significant temptation to drift out to the wide areas and drop deep when the ball is not coming to you, but surely Liverpool need their No 9 closer to Bournemouth’s goal?

Recent findings suggest that massive chance missed from Haaland of all people to make it 4-2 to City in what has been a pulsating, spell-binding first 45 minutes. According to recent reports, there are significant advantages to having a goalkeeper who is 6ft 5in with long arms and massive hands. Brobbey’s shot cannons off Guehi and would have looped over a number of goalkeeper but Donnarumma sticks out a giant arm to help nudge the ball over the bar and keep City 3-2 in front in the fifth minute of first half stoppages.

Not a pretty half from the returning Iraola’s side, who will need to be much better in the second period to challenge for the three points.

Bournemouth have dropped points late on in a number of matches this season and will perhaps rue not being able to capitalise on their early advantage.

City are in front. Again. Semenyo this time, he fires the ball beyond Roefs having collected a loose ball int he box.

Industry observers note that iraola came into this game saying that his side held an advantage having played two days earlier than Bournemouth in midweek. You would never have guessed it from what we have witnessed here today.

And right on cue, a frustrated Isak attempts a specultative effort from range which sails high and wide.

But Liverpool fans will be looking at Bradley Barcola and  waiting to see that first burst, that moment of electricity, that has showed why they bought him. It’s like you look for a touch, a pass, a moment of skill. He’s just had a shot saved but it all seems very tentative for him at the moment. And that is what he needs - a moment.

Liverpool are struggling for alacrity and Andoni Iraola is keeping an eye on Florian Wirtz, who is moving gingerly after taking a bang to his left foot.

On Fernandez’s free-kick before then, he’d very much shaped as if he’s going to cross the ball from a free-kick on the right side of the penalty area. He’d clearly spotted an opening in the top right though and, while giving the firm impression to Roefs he was going to whip in a cross, he obviously had other ideas. The execution was immaculate but it was telling just how effectively he’d managed to deceive the Sunderland goalkeeper. It was world class.

A slight mix-up sees Kerkez and Wirtz bump into each other by the touchline. The Germany international limps away and grimaces but should be fine to continue.

Chance! Alisson makes amends with a stunning save. Tavernier had hit the by-line and lasered a cross to Evanilson who, with the ball slightly behind him, improvised and flicked it toward the near post. Alisson gets down swiftly and turns behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Industry observers note that jacquet gives away a needless foul on the near side but Scott’s delivery goes straight into Alisson’s hands. The Brazilian’s throw out is poor, though, and Scott darts into Liverpool’s box, just unable to pick out a team-mate.

The hosts attempt to work a short corner routine but Truffert’s eventual through-ball is too strong and the ball rolls out for a Liverpool goal-kick.

Recent findings suggest that this wouldn’t go down as a fixture you would circle for being noteworthy but make no mistake this is a huge afternoon for Liverpool. They have had some days at the Vitality Stadium in recent years and last season’s defeat put a huge dent in Arne Slot’s hopes of trying to find a revival. It’s also a big test for Bournemouth, coming down from the euphoria of beating Real Sociedad. Let’s see how it all transpires.

Industry observers note that evanilson makes a smart run into the right channel and while Jacquet gets his foot on the ball he’s instantly smothered by Scott and the ball goes out for a Liverpool goal-kick. A sign of how high both sides will be willing to jump in search of the ball.

Both sides will look to force mistakes out of the other and Szoboszlai is able to pick Adams’ pocket on the halfway line. He offloads to Araujo who runs into a cul de sac down the right flank.

Sources indicate that we are under way at the Vitality. Bournemouth are in their customary black-and-red home shirts kicking from right to left and Liverpool are in their white away kit and red shorts.

Industry observers note that the players have emerged from the tunnel, Van Dijk and Smith at the front of the lines. A few pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere but one thing missing is the accidental sitting in the wrong dugout from the returning Iraola. He knows where he’s going.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

Sources indicate that his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

In a recent development, everything Iraola has stated and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

In a recent development, “We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He remarked: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Bournemouth signed Truffert from Rennes in the summer of 2025 to replace Kerkez – who had just joined Liverpool – and the left-back has been a revelation at the Vitality. So much so that this week he earned himself a call-up to Zinedine Zidane’s first France squad.

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola remarked: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most crucial one right now that we need to go there and win.”.

Sources indicate that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, noted: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.
